name: Aadhaar / PAN / OTP passed in URL query string
attack_scenario: The Aadhaar/PAN/OTP appears in access logs, proxy caches, analytics, and the Referer sent to third-party scripts on the next page; anyone reading those logs or the referring host harvests the identifiers and one-time codes, enabling KYC fraud and OTP replay before expiry.
negative_test_hint: request the KYC status URL with query string "aadhaar=123456789012&otp=482913" and assert the identifiers travel in the POST body instead and never appear in access logs or the Referer header

exemplar.explanation: Query strings are recorded by web servers, proxies, CDNs, and browser history and leak to third parties via the Referer header, so carrying Aadhaar, PAN, or OTP values in a URL exposes them to anyone reading those logs and enables OTP replay before expiry. Sending the same values in a POST request body keeps them out of URLs and logs.
